market.name: AI Scientists (Global)
market.tagline: AI systems that run the research loop: hypothesis, experiment, result, repeat.
market.definition: Companies building AI that conducts scientific research itself, from proposing hypotheses and running computational or robotic lab experiments to analysing results and deciding what to try next.
market.allDescription: Compare research autonomy, scientific range and access across the full landscape.
market.author: Shamkhal Murtazaaliev
market.scope: Companies worldwide, judged on the same criteria; each profile gives the headquarters.
inclusion: Runs research steps itself: proposes, runs and learns from experiments, computational or physical
Aimed at discovery: new findings in science or AI research, not writing help or search
A company or product line pursuing it, not a one-off paper
exclusions: AI design tools that propose candidates but leave the experiments to people
Lab-automation hardware without an AI that plans experiments

judgedExcluded.name: CuspAI
judgedExcluded.why: Cambridge (UK) AI materials-design platform, reported to have raised about $450M in 2026; it proposes candidate materials, with validation through partners rather than its own experimental loop

judgedExcluded.name: FutureHouse
judgedExcluded.why: Non-profit lab whose AI scientist work, including Kosmos, moved to its for-profit spinout Edison Scientific

judgedExcluded.name: Elicit
judgedExcluded.why: Research assistant that searches and summarizes papers for people; it does not run experiments

judgedExcluded.name: Harmonic
judgedExcluded.why: Builds Aristotle, an AI mathematician that proves theorems; it works on formal proofs, not experiments

judgedExcluded.name: NeoCognition
judgedExcluded.why: Raised a $40M seed in April 2026 for general agents that learn like humans, not scientific research

judgedExcluded.name: Tetsuwan Scientific
judgedExcluded.why: San Francisco robotic-lab startup ($2.7M pre-seed, 2024) still building toward AI that plans experiments; too early to place

x.label: Research autonomy
x.rubric: 0 = helps a person with one research step, such as searching the literature or analysing data; 25 = runs several steps, such as reviewing literature, proposing hypotheses and analysing results, that a scientist directs; 50 = runs a full computational research cycle, from hypothesis through in-silico experiments to a written report, for people to review; 75 = closes the loop with physical experiments in automated labs, choosing the next experiment from the last result while people set goals; 100 = runs open-ended research programs on its own, choosing problems, running lab experiments and reporting validated discoveries

y.label: Scientific range
y.rubric: 0 = one assay, problem type or dataset; 25 = one subfield, such as machine-learning research, protein design or battery materials; 50 = one science, such as biology, chemistry or materials; 75 = several sciences; 100 = any science, from physics to medicine

yAlt.label: Access
yAlt.rubric: 0 = used only for the company's own discoveries; 25 = partnerships and pilots by arrangement; 50 = a product researchers can apply for or use in preview; 75 = a generally available paid product or API; 100 = open source that anyone can run

categories.name: Lab in the loop
categories.description: AI scientists that run physical experiments in automated or robotic labs.

categories.name: Computational
categories.description: AI scientists that work in code and data: hypotheses, analyses and in-silico experiments.

companies.name: Lila Sciences
companies.description: Flagship Pioneering company building what it calls scientific superintelligence: AI that generates hypotheses, designs and runs experiments in its own autonomous labs, and learns from the new data in real time, across life sciences, chemistry and materials.
companies.traction: Offers enterprise access to its platform and co-creation partnerships across therapeutics, advanced materials, chemicals, energy and other industries.

autonomy.rationale: AI agents propose experiments that run in its robotic labs, with results feeding back into the models.

range.rationale: Life sciences, chemistry, materials and energy.

access.rationale: Enterprise access and partnerships by arrangement.

lastRound.note: The extension valued Lila at more than $1.3B. Bloomberg reported in June 2026 that it was in talks to raise about $2B at roughly $8.5B before the new money; no close has been announced.

news.title: Lila Sciences said in talks for funds at $8.5 billion valuation
AI lab Lila Sciences tops $1.3 billion valuation with new Nvidia backing

companies.name: Periodic Labs
companies.description: AI research company building AI scientists and the autonomous labs for them to work in, starting with materials: robots mix and heat candidate materials, instruments measure the results, and those measurements become training data that internet text cannot provide.

founders.name: Ekin Dogus Cubuk
founders.role: Co-founder; led Google DeepMind's GNoME materials project

companies.traction: Its $300M seed was reported as the largest of 2025.

autonomy.rationale: Autonomous labs run and measure experiments whose results train its models.

range.rationale: Materials science, with chemistry and physics around it.

access.rationale: Used for its own research; partners by arrangement.

lastRound.note: The $7.5B is from Forbes, which reported in May 2026 that Periodic was in advanced talks to raise at least $500M at that valuation; the close has not been confirmed. Sources differ on whether a16z or Felicis led the seed.

news.title: Former OpenAI researcher to raise $500 million for AI science startup
Periodic Labs launches with $300M to build an "AI scientist"

companies.name: Medra
companies.description: Builds the Physical AI Scientist: robotic workcells that run a lab's own protocols on its own instruments, with AI that turns text into protocols, detects and recovers from errors with computer vision, and optimizes experiments in a closed loop.
companies.traction: The Series A funds a fully autonomous lab in San Francisco opening in 2026.

autonomy.rationale: Runs protocols autonomously and optimizes them in a closed loop; scientists still choose the questions.

access.rationale: Deployed with biotech customers by arrangement.

lastRound.note: The $52M Series A was publicly reported; its December 11, 2025 date, the investor list and the $63M total funding were entered manually from a source that is not public. Some participants were not named. Valuation not disclosed.

news.title: Medra raises $52M Series A to build autonomous AI scientists that run lab experiments at scale

companies.name: Radical AI
companies.description: Autonomous materials discovery: scientists enter performance goals, AI generates experiments that go straight to its self-driving lab, and results feed back into the models until the material meets the goals.
companies.traction: Opened New York's first fully autonomous materials science lab at the Brooklyn Navy Yard in January 2026.

autonomy.rationale: AI-generated experiments run in its self-driving lab and iterate until goals are met.

lastRound.note: A later Series A of about $60M has been reported but not confirmed. Valuation not disclosed.

news.title: Governor Hochul celebrates Radical AI establishing New York's first fully autonomous materials science labs at the Brooklyn Navy Yard

companies.name: Chemify
companies.description: Chemputation: programmable chemistry that combines robotic synthesis, computation, machine learning and its own chemical programming language to discover and make new molecules and materials, in a research centre and production "Chemifarm" in Glasgow.

founders.name: Lee Cronin
founders.role: Founder & CEO; Regius Professor of Chemistry, University of Glasgow

companies.traction: Secured about £22M in Scottish and UK government grants in September 2026 to triple its Glasgow workforce to about 450.

autonomy.rationale: Robotic synthesis driven by code and machine learning closes the loop on making molecules.

lastRound.note: The $145.73M post-money valuation and the $120.65M total funding were entered manually from a source that is not public. Round stage, date and investors are not public.

companies.name: Edison Scientific
companies.description: For-profit spinout of the non-profit FutureHouse. Its Kosmos AI scientist reads literature, analyses data, generates and branches hypotheses and steers investigations mid-run, running hundreds of research tasks in parallel, deployed across biopharma R&D.
companies.traction: Announced a partnership with Incyte; customers include biopharma companies and academic institutions. Kosmos can be tried on its platform.

autonomy.rationale: Runs full computational investigations, from literature and data analysis to hypotheses and reports, for scientists to review.

range.rationale: Biology and medicine first, with work across other data-rich sciences.

access.rationale: Kosmos is a paid product researchers can use, plus enterprise deployments.

lastRound.note: Some outlets call the round a Series A. A biotech investor co-led alongside the two named firms.

news.title: Edison Scientific raises $70M to build autonomous AI scientists for research

companies.name: Autoscience
companies.description: Automated AI research lab: its AI scientists, led by the agent Carl, design, run and write up machine-learning research, and it deploys them as managed services to improve enterprise models.
companies.traction: Says Carl authored the first largely AI-written paper accepted through academic peer review, at an ICLR 2025 workshop.

autonomy.rationale: Runs computational research cycles end to end, from ideas to experiments and papers.

access.rationale: Managed services for selected large companies.

news.title: Autoscience builds automated research lab for machine learning models with $14M

companies.name: Drylab
companies.description: Singapore startup founded by a Vietnamese team, building an AI research platform for biomedical scientists: autonomous agents that carry out computational analyses from start to finish and capture each lab's workflows and decisions so every analysis improves the next.
companies.traction: Operates in Singapore and San Francisco. PatSnap joined the seed and will support its life sciences work.

autonomy.rationale: Runs computational research from start to finish for pharma teams to review.

news.title: Vietnamese-founded Drylab bags US$3M to put autonomous AI scientists inside pharma labs

companies.name: Google AI co-scientist
companies.description: Multi-agent Gemini system from Google DeepMind that generates, debates and evolves research hypotheses with a scientist, described in Nature; available as an experimental Hypothesis Generation tool and through Gemini for Science.
companies.parent: Alphabet — public (NASDAQ: GOOGL). Co-Scientist is a Google DeepMind research product; the parent's market capitalization is not a standalone product valuation.
companies.traction: Opened to individual researchers in May 2026; scientists at all 17 US Department of Energy national laboratories get accelerated access.

autonomy.rationale: Generates and ranks hypotheses for a scientist to test; it does not run the experiments.

access.rationale: Experimental tool for registered researchers and partners, with no public pricing.

news.title: Co-Scientist: A multi-agent AI partner to accelerate research

companies.name: The AI Scientist (Sakana AI)
companies.description: Open-source system from Tokyo's Sakana AI that automates machine-learning research end to end: it generates ideas, writes and runs experiment code, evaluates results and drafts papers with minimal human direction; a second version followed.
companies.parent: Sakana AI — private Tokyo AI company, valued at about $2.6B after a $135M Series B in November 2025. The AI Scientist is one open-source research system; the company's valuation is not a standalone figure for it.
companies.traction: Code released openly on GitHub; a paper written by its second version passed peer review at an ICLR 2025 workshop.

autonomy.rationale: Runs a full computational research cycle, from idea to paper.

access.rationale: Open source that anyone can run.

news.title: The AI Scientist: Towards fully automated open-ended scientific discovery
